title: Temporary weight decay and momentum under shuffling
subtitle: Muon pretraining · without-replacement finite sums · inference compute · randomized labels
intro: Two new papers examine how weight norms carry the effect of early decay and why momentum in without-replacement training depends on the problem. Briefs cover multi-agent budget comparisons and the form of pretraining data. The classic revisits randomized labels.

blocks.text: The intervention applies decoupled weight decay to hidden weight matrices during a short window. Early decay reduces weight norms, while Muon normalizes matrix update norms. Once decay ends, the runs follow the same update rule, but smaller weights still take larger steps relative to their size. [1]

blocks.text: After decay ends, suppose consecutive updates have approximately equal Frobenius norms. Let a be update norm divided by weight norm, and κ the weight–update inner product divided by squared update norm. Expanding the squared weight norm yields the recurrence below. Similar κ trajectories imply a slowly changing gap in inverse squared relative step sizes. [1]

blocks.text: A decay window covering the first 44% of steps, selected at 162M, was transferred directly to 1.4B (FineWeb100B, 28,000 updates). Its validation loss was 0.26 nats above no decay when the window ended. It crossed the baseline at 73% of training and finished 0.0275 nats lower. A separate comparison fixes the window at the first 10% of training. [1]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Norm resets at 162M and 405M support weight norm as the mediator of most of the gain. The recurrence describes persistent step-size differences. Final loss is measured in the training comparisons. [1]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Complexity counts individual component updates. The counterexample holds for every permutation when the step size within an epoch is constant and at most 1/(2N). It limits a universal choice of fixed momentum. [2]

blocks.text: The authors distinguish memorizing category properties, generalizing to new entities, and applying knowledge in context. They analyze open models on 199 category–feature pairs and train a 68M model from scratch with controlled data expressions. The abstract reports that exact repetition reduces flexible use, while mixing different forms of expression improves it. [5]

classic.evidence: Read §§2 and 4, Table 1, and Appendix C. Conference record [7].
classic.question: With architecture, initialization distribution, and optimizer fixed, what measurable complexity of the trained predictor would track interpolation and generalization as the randomized-label fraction changes?

blocks.text: The paper compares the same network trained with true labels and fixed random labels. On CIFAR-10, Inception without data augmentation or weight decay reached 100% training accuracy in both cases. Its test accuracies were 85.75% and 9.78%, respectively. This comparison separates fitting the sample from generalizing beyond it. [6]
